title: Sarah Paine: the Risk of Nuclear War, WW3 and NATO [INTERVIEW]
summary: A naval historian warns the world is heading toward a nuclear world war, says a US seizure of Greenland would wreck NATO, and says Russia is already waging sabotage against Europe but is too stretched to fight it.

assertions.quote: Yeah, I I think we're barreling our way towards one.

verdicts.note: Forecasters and base rates put a direct US-Russia or US-China war within a few years well under even odds, even though the risk is elevated.

assertions.quote: The loser, if they have a nuclear weapon, is going to fling it before they lose.

verdicts.note: Nuclear powers have lost or retreated without using them (the US in Vietnam, the Soviets in Afghanistan, Israel's early 1973 setbacks, Russia in 2022).

For Russia, RAND says a desperate situation threatening regime survival could make nuclear use the best of bad options, yet even then 'Russia may well avoid such highly consequential actions'; it is a risk, not a rule.

assertions.quote: it'll be climate change but it'll be called nuclear winter
the United States is never going to be given three years to get its act together.

verdicts.note: No war between nuclear powers has been fought, so whether escalation would outrun industrial mobilisation cannot be tested.

assertions.quote: It will blow NATO, the American participation in NATO.

verdicts.note: A counterfactual about an event that has not happened.

assertions.quote: They're already doing all of that. They're already they're in a sense they already are at war with Europe.
The guy is already overextended exactly where he is.
this sharing of intelligence that took away the whole false flag stuff and made it clear that it was naked Russian aggression

verdicts.note: The disclosures undercut Russian false-flag pretexts and rallied allies, but Ukraine's survival owed more to its forces and Russian planning failures.

assertions.quote: this would be why you need to build up your defense industry

verdicts.note: EU rearmament plans since 2025 explicitly aim to reduce reliance on US weapons amid doubts about US commitment, though Russia is the main threat cited.
Fleck describes Europe facing a new era without predictable US support and answering with Rearm Europe 2030, an 800-billion-euro defence package and Germany's half-trillion-euro surge.

SIPRI links European spending to uncertainty over US guarantees and notes France aims for an 'economy prepared for war' by 2030 with mostly domestic equipment; reliance on the US is one driver among others, not shown to be the cause.
DDIS says the US shift toward the Pacific creates greater demand for European rearmament and cooperation to deter Russia, which is doubt about US reliance rather than an inability to rely on it.
The Munich Security Report says Europeans, facing shifting US signals, are preparing for greater autonomy while trying to keep the US engaged; it does not single out the defence industry.
